output.methodChoice: Compared the score drop by floor block and date against the engineering, verbatim, telemetry, and rate records; collected X9 (corridor temperatures) and X5 (rate and occupancy) and no others.
output.brief: The August dip is almost entirely a floors 6-8 problem caused by the chiller CH-2 failure. It ran from 4 to 19 August, and corridor temperatures there reached 27-30 C against a set point of 22. Guest complaints about heat (56 of the 74 negative comments) line up with that window, and scores recovered after the repair on 19 August. Floors 1-5, which had the same rate rise and the same contractor and kiosk changes, held steady. So the housekeeping contractor and the kiosks are not the cause, and I would not serve notice on Orrin or pull the kiosks on this evidence. The rate rise may have added to the value-for-money dip, but the data cannot separate it from the usual seasonal dip, so I rate that link as uncertain. Next steps: reschedule the deferred maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and set a written cooling-outage recovery procedure. Do not exclude the August floors 6-8 responses from the score. Confidence is high on the chiller cause, moderate on the rate question.
